name: Isolated Focal Cortical Dysplasia Type Ic

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: International League Against Epilepsy (ILAE) Classification for Focal Cortical Dysplasia

criteria.description: Histopathological confirmation of isolated cortical dyslamination without dysmorphic neurons or balloon cells
MRI evidence of focal cortical thickening or blurring of the gray-white matter junction localized to a single cortical area
Focal epilepsy with seizure semiology consistent with cortical origin corresponding to imaging findings

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation plus MRI evidence of focal cortical dysplasia and clinical seizure pattern consistent with lesion location
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary evaluation including neuropathology, neuroimaging, and clinical correlation.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Focal onset seizures with impaired awareness
Epileptiform discharges localized to dysplastic cortex on EEG
searchTerms: seizure activity seen on EEG in abnormal cortex
epileptic discharges in dysplastic brain region
EEG showing seizures in malformed cortex
focal epilepsy not responding to drugs

common.symptomName: Cognitive impairment related to epileptogenic zone
searchTerms: thinking problems linked to seizure area
cognitive issues from epileptic brain zone
mental impairment related to seizure focus
sensory or autonomic aura before seizures
warning signs involving senses or body functions

occasional.symptomName: Mood disturbances including anxiety or depression

searchTerms: head pain during or after seizures

occasional.symptomName: Mild developmental delay in early onset cases

rare.symptomName: Focal neurological deficits unrelated to seizures
searchTerms: localized neurological problems not caused by seizures
focal nerve deficits unrelated to epilepsy
specific neurological symptoms separate from seizures

rare.symptomName: Visual field deficits due to occipital lobe involvement
searchTerms: vision loss from occipital brain damage
visual field defects due to back brain involvement

imaging: MRI showing focal cortical thickening and blurring of gray-white matter junction
High-resolution MRI with FLAIR hyperintensity in affected cortex
genetic: Somatic mutations in mTOR pathway genes (e.g., MTOR, DEPDC5) identified in some cases
other: Electroencephalogram (EEG) demonstrating focal epileptiform discharges concordant with lesion

distinguishingFeatures: Multisystem involvement with skin, renal, and cardiac lesions
Multiple cortical tubers rather than isolated focal lesion
Genetic mutations in TSC1 or TSC2 genes
Presence of dysmorphic neurons on histopathology
More prominent epileptogenicity and often larger lesions
Different MRI characteristics including transmantle sign

redFlags: New onset focal seizures in infancy or early childhood
Progressive neurological deficits or developmental regression
references: Blumcke I, et al. The clinicopathologic spectrum of focal cortical dysplasias: a consensus classification proposed by an ad hoc Task Force of the ILAE Diagnostic Methods Commission. Epilepsia. 2011 Jun;52(6):158-174.
Aronica E, et al. Focal cortical dysplasia: neuropathological subtypes, EEG, and MRI correlations. Epilepsia. 2012;53 Suppl 4:23-28.
